name: bounding_box_of_two_far_bodies
why: Two bodies 600 mm apart: each fits in 100x100x20, and the box that contains both of them is 620 high. It is the difference between «how big is the body» and «how much space does the part take up», and on a weldment it is the question that counts. If the union of the boxes were wrong, the number would come out equal to that of a single body -- believable, and wrong by thirty times.

expect.tolerance_why: from z = 0 to z = 620: the second body starts at 600 and is 20 thick
the single body has stayed what it was
asking for ONE body gets the answer for that one, and the 620 disappears

the bounding box alone is blind to WHICH body (they are equal): it is the position that tells. Entry Z-C16: on 25/9/2026 one run in three «C1» was the copy, at z 600, and the case was green just the same. Now the body is named by name and we check that it starts from z = 0
